questions.question: D, E, F, G, M, N and O are sitting around a circular table, facing the centre of the table. Only E sits between N and M. M sits third to the left of O. G sits to the immediate left of O. D is not an immediate neighbour of M. Who sits third to the left of F?
questions.solution:
**Given:** D, E, F, G, M, N and O are sitting around a circular table, facing the centre of the table.

1) M sits third to the left of O.

2) G sits to the immediate left of O.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/5b7b763ae0b793fe2aa12cf403dabae67371bdb9a22f33bd30f79090418aaad7.png] 

3) Only E sits between N and M.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/bb3ca7fe2a0f42fe525c8cf9fcfe16f2f8727a5e80fabcb95e68442c8219a505.png] 

4) D is not an immediate neighbour of M. 

After positioning D only one position is left which will be occupied by the only person left i.e. F.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/53f79e7ddb67a4edbb5dfbd3fd461e9f408fe55b3b7ad06b9ecd027c1929f6ed.png] 

Thus, N sits third to the left of F.

Hence, **"Option 2"** is the correct answer.

questions.question: Mr. O starts from Point L and drives 3 km towards the south. He then takes a left turn, drives 3 km, turns right and drives 4 km. He then takes a left turn and drives 4 km. He takes a final left turn, drives 7 km and stops at Point M. How far (shortest distance) and towards which direction should he drive in order to reach Point L again? (All turns are 90 degree turns only unless specified.)
questions.solution:
Given: 

Mr. O starts from Point L and drives 3 km towards the south.

He then takes a left turn, drives 3 km, turns right and drives 4 km.

He then takes a left turn and drives 4 km.

He takes a final left turn, drives 7 km and stops at Point M.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/539559cd3b2c2e2fb2ecbf5101a9bddfdf74a8198e0a62fee5f764ad791c7ae0.png] 

Thus, Mr. O should drive 7 km (3 km + 4 km) in the west direction in order to reach Point L again.

Hence, **"Option 1"** is the correct answer.

questions.question: Shubham ranked 19th from the top and 46th from the bottom in his class. How many students are there in his class?
questions.solution:
**Given:** Shubham ranked 19th from the top and 46th from the bottom in his class.

Shubham's rank from the top = 19

Shubham's rank from the bottom = 46

Total students = Shubham's rank from the top + Shubham's rank from the bottom - 1

= 19 + 46 - 1 → 64

Hence, "Option 4" is the correct answer.
